title: feat: let models require prompt safety
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Stores required safety once on the shared community model listing
- Applies the same policy to proxy models, prompt agents, and endpoint agents
- Lets providers configure it through the API, dashboard, or CLI
- Unions model and fallback requirements so callers cannot disable checks
- Keeps cache entries isolated by the effective safety policy

Supersedes #14292 after its head ref stopped synchronizing.

gist.headline: Safety sticks to the model
gist.blurb: Community models can now carry their own prompt-safety requirements, wherever they travel in the hive. Proxy models, agents, fallbacks, caches: nobody accidentally leaves the guardrails in the garden shed.
gist.summary: Added provider-configurable required prompt-safety policies to shared community model listings, applying them consistently to proxy models, prompt and endpoint agents, fallbacks, and policy-isolated caches.
gist.impact: Providers can set a model's safety requirements through the API, dashboard, or Polli CLI, and callers receive the union of model and fallback policies without being able to disable those checks.
gist.visual_concept: Depict model safety as a small garden gate or protective glass terrarium attached directly to labeled code-plants, rather than a removable checkpoint. Polli, wearing a tiny ranger hat, tends the plants while a CRT monitor robot carries policy cards between a community-model signpost, agent terminals, and a fallback path, showing that every route inherits the same protection.
gist.image_prompt: A cozy pixel-art community model garden where prompt-safety shields are permanently tied around lime green (#ecf874) code-plants, with safe paths leading to a proxy terminal, tiny agent workstations, and a fallback flower bed; Polli is a cute pixel bee mascot with a yellow body, dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular cheek blushes, a small happy smile, rounded translucent light-blue wings, and a tiny ranger hat, warmly checking the shared safety gate beside an eager CRT-monitor robot holding policy cards. Cozy 8-bit pixel art aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes like Stardew Valley or A Short Hike, subtle CRT glow, pixel-font sign reading "SAFETY STAYS", nostalgic and emotionally warm.
